chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no cutting (of the hand) for a feather, meaning the whole bird.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir Al-Momineen (Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.رِيش: Feather (referring to the value or type of property)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hand for stealing a bird in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply to stealing birds, as their value is considered minimal (below the nisab threshold). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of property valuation in Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing between significant assets and those of lesser worth. It underscores the principle that legal penalties must be proportionate to the value of the stolen item.
